Welcome to Canbury School
Welcome to Canbury School – inclusive independent co-educational school for students aged 11 to 18
Welcome to Canbury School, where we have been providing a nurturing and inclusive secondary education since 1982.
With a maximum of just 76 students and small class sizes, we offer a uniquely supportive environment tailored to the individual needs of our students. Whether supporting students with autism, ADHD, or specific learning needs like dyslexia and dyspraxia, our dedicated team of teachers, therapists, and pastoral specialists work collaboratively to ensure every child thrives.
While we provide the broad curriculum of a mainstream school, including GCSEs, BTECs, and Level 1 and 2 courses, our small-scale, bespoke approach ensures that each student receives the personalised attention they need to reach their full potential.
An accepting, creative and aspirational place of learning where difference is celebrated.
Recent News
Testimonials
We honestly are so grateful that we found you at the right time - Canbury School has made a huge difference to our son's life and helped him get back on track. The kind and caring environment has been truly transformational and we can now see all the potential in him, that was completely missed by his previous school. Thank you so so much for everything you have done. We will always remember this time at Canbury as a turning point in his life

Senior Welcome Mornings
Visit Us
The transition from Year 6 into Year 7 is probably one of the biggest steps that your child will make to date in their educational journey. To ensure that this transition is smooth we will be hosting three Senior Welcome Mornings over the coming months. As this transition is so important we feel it is vital to start the process for many children in year 5. The date of each event is listed below:
At Canbury School our aim is to provide as many opportunities as possible to ensure students achieve their full potential, both academically and personally; this starts with our Senior Welcome Mornings. This is an informal assessment approach for entry to the school. The students experience a range of subjects across the curriculum as well as the atmosphere at Canbury; this enables us to get to know our potential students. The students also build friendships with each other which allow them to start at Canbury in Year 7 with an existing friendship group in place.
To book a place at the Senior Welcome Morning, please contact the school Registrar via email at [email protected] or phone us on 0208 549 8622.
Recent News

Drama
Drama is for everyone, even if you do not like performing in front of an audience.
This year, Drama has introduced a theory side to its curriculum that involves students learning about the ‘other side’ of Drama. This may include aspects such as lighting, costume and make up design that will help students understand the bigger picture to Drama, rather than just the acting side of this subject.
The theory side will call upon creative students to get an in-depth look into the things that happen behind the camera! Have no fear… the students that do enjoy performing will still have the opportunity to take part in script work or devising their own plays to ensure that everyone has an opportunity to take part.
Students in Key Stage 3 have a 1-hour lesson a week in this subject.
LAMDA club is offered to the whole school and is run during a lunch break one day a week.
To find out more about LAMDA click HERE

Music
Music
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.
Music is all-inclusive. Pupils will gain an understanding and acceptance of the validity and importance of all types of music, and an unbiased respect for the role that music may wish to be expressed in any person’s life. It is widely known that Music has a very positive impact on our mental health. Listening to music can change our mood and help us reflect on our feelings and experiences. Actually making music can help deepen that process, and making music with others brings further, overlapping, social, emotional – and educational – benefits. Music is deeply rooted in our evolution as a species – it’s no surprise that scientists have found that no other activity connects and activates so many different parts of the brain

Art, Craft and Design / Photography
Art, Craft and Design / Photography
We aim to create a safe and stimulating environment where we can cater for students of all abilities and value all the work created. We want our students to be independent, creative and not afraid to try out new ideas.
We offer students the opportunity to experience a wide variety of media and techniques in a range of disciplines and materials, such as painting and drawing, three-dimensions, mixed media, graphic design, ICT, textiles, animation and digital photography.
Students in Year 7, 8 and 9 have 2-hour lessons each week.
GCSE students are time tabled for 3 one-hour lessons per week. Students in Year 10 work on a variety of projects where they explore and develop their skills with a wide range of media, techniques, processes and materials, enabling students to discover their particular strengths.
In the Autumn term, Year 11 students respond to a number of themes that they select from a given range. This promotes independence and fosters an understanding of the requirements needed for success in the summer exam.
We offer GCSE Art, Craft and Design and GCSE Photography.
A number of departmental trips throughout the year help students gather inspiration for their projects; previous ones have included visits to Kew Gardens, The Tate Modern, The Victoria and Albert Museum, The National Portrait Gallery and Brighton.
The department encourages the use and development of ICT skills.
Recent News

English
English
English is a core subject at Canbury and studied by all students in Key Stages 3 and 4.
Throughout Key Stage 3, students study a range of thought-provoking novels, poems and plays which inspire curious thinking and discussion. They also explore a range of non-fiction texts from the 19th century and modern day, which encourages an appreciation of language and how it has evolved.
Students are encouraged to read and to bring a book to school – or borrow one from our small but diverse library!
All schemes of work in Key Stage 3 cover vital and relevant skills required for success at the GCSE course. It is through the gradual building of these skills that students develop confidence and make progress.
In Key Stage 4, students work towards the AQA English Language GCSE, which is assessed through two final examination papers at the end of Year 11. They also complete a Spoken Language component, which is a compulsory element of the GCSE Language examination and awarded by an additional credit on their examination certificate.
English Literature is offered as an optional subject, which students can choose in Year 9 as part of their GCSE Options.
Pupils not following a GCSE pathway will study Functional Skills English at Levels 1 and 2.

Geography
Geography
Geography is the explanation of the world around us, and the study of Geography can underpin and explain the physical, human, environmental and geopolitical workings of the world. As we all know, the world is complex, and constantly changing. Studying Geography allows young people to begin to make sense of the world.
It explains where places are, how places and landscapes are formed, how people and their environment interact, and how a diverse range of economies, societies and environments are interconnected.
Geography builds on students’ own experiences to investigate places at all scales, from the personal to the global, and includes case studies throughout all years. As students’ progress, they will gain geographical knowledge, understanding and skills that will help them to explain how features of both human and physical geography are shaped, interconnected and changed over time.
In Key Stage 3 students will study units including:
Becoming a Geographer
Mapping and Geographical Skills
People Around the World
Climate Change
Development and Almighty Dollar
Coastal Geography
Rivers and Flooding
Tectonic Processes
In Key Stage 4 students will study towards the EdExcel ‘Geography B’ specification:
Students study towards three different papers, and undertake both physical and human fieldwork.
Geography is highly respected by employers, and due to the wide knowledge and skills learned through Geography, Geography students have one of the highest rates of graduate employment, pursuing a wide range of career paths.

History
History
The History Department aims to foster a love of the past in all students and to help them develop an understanding of what happened, why and with what consequences. Students will develop a range of skills through the use and evaluation of historical source material, extended writing and oral work.
Key Stage 3 (Years 7, 8 and 9)
In Year 7 students begin with a look at how we know about the past and build on their previous experience of History by studying Anglo-Saxon Britain, setting the scene for the Norman invasion. They then move on to investigate what life was like for the ordinary people in Medieval England followed by an assessment of our Medieval monarchs with a particular focus on William I, Henry II, John and Richard III.
In Year 8 students study Britain 1500-1750 looking especially at the religious and political changes of the Tudor and Stuart period. This is followed by a study of Black People of the Americas from slavery to Civil Rights.
In Year 9 students study Britain 1750-1900, focusing on the Industrial Revolution and its consequences for the nation. This is followed by an investigation of aspects of 20th Century World History including the causes and consequences of the two world wars.
Key Stage 4 (Years 10 and 11)
The IGCSE is made up of two units:
The twentieth century: international relations since1919 covering topics such as the Treaty of Versailles, the League of Nations, the causes of World War II and the Cold War including US involvement in the Korean War, the Cuban Missile Crisis and Vietnam. We will also study the USSR’s control over Eastern Europe, 1948-c.1989. Germany 1918-1945 covering topics such as the Weimar Republic, the rise of Hitler and what it was like to live under Nazi rule.
Studying IGCSE History will enable the student to explore topics that will be new to them from the 20th Century, whilst at the same time revisiting some favourites from Key Stage 3.

Mathematics
Mathematics
Studying maths helps us find patterns and structure in our lives. Practically, maths helps us put a price on things, create graphics , build websites, build skyscrapers and generally understand how things work or predict how they might change over time and under different conditions.
The aim of the Mathematics department at Canbury School is to help students develop their knowledge, skills, enjoyment and understanding of mathematical concepts. This will help them develop the knowledge to tackle scientific, mechanical, coding and abstract problems, and develop logic to tackle everyday issues like planning projects, managing budgets and even debating effectively.
The Mathematics course at Canbury School is designed to cover all areas of the National Curriculum, including Number, Algebra, Shape, Space, Measure, Statistics, Probability, Using and applying Mathematics. At Key Stage 4 students work towards completing either the Edexcel iGCSE in Mathematics (Foundation or Higher level) qualification or for those for whom iGCSE Maths is not the most appropriate pathway the department offers Pearson Functional Skills at Entry Level 3 and Levels 1 & 2 at the end of Year 11. Students also have the opportunity to choose to study for Edexcel GCSE Statistics in Key Stage 4. This requires extra study out of normal school hours.
All students have 4 Mathematics lessons a week and have access to a variety of different websites including My Maths, Dr Frost Maths, Diagnostic Questions and IXL.com which contain additional support and lessons. They also have the opportunity to attend a weekly lunchtime clinic where students can bring their maths homework, or something they have been struggling with, or just do maths for fun.

PSHE
Empowering our Students
At Canbury School, our mission is to prepare students not just for exams, but for life. Our PSHE and RSE curriculum is designed to give your child the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need to lead safe, healthy, and fulfilling lives in an ever-changing world.
What is PSHE & RSE?
These lessons provide a supportive space for students to explore essential life themes at an age-appropriate level.
Our Approach: Partnership with Parents
We believe that parents are the first teachers of these subjects. Our school curriculum is designed to complement and support the conversations you are already having at home.
Our Goal: To foster resilient, kind, and informed young people who have the self-esteem to make positive choices for themselves and others.
“Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.” — Nelson Mandela

Wellbeing
Our Year 7 and 8 Wellbeing Curriculum is designed to equip students with essential skills for emotional regulation, social understanding, and personal growth.
Key Focus Areas: Year 7: Mastering Emotional Intelligence
Students are introduced to the Zones of Regulation framework to help them identify, understand, and communicate their emotions. We focus on developing social awareness, recognising non-verbal communication, and understanding the impact of expected and unexpected behaviours. The year culminates in building a wellbeing toolbox, exploring sensory supports, and learning thinking strategies like ‘Size of a Problem’ and developing the Inner Coach to manage challenging emotions (Yellow Zone tools).
Year 8: Cultivating Resilience and Mindfulness
The focus shifts to Growth Mindset, exploring the brain’s plasticity and the importance of effort, mistakes, and feedback for success.
This curriculum provides the foundation for self-awareness and positive mental health, ensuring students have the strategies needed to navigate the challenges of adolescence and beyond.

Business Studies
Business Studies
The OCR GCSE Business Studies course aims develop students’ knowledge and understanding of business theory and practice as well as develop the essential analysis and communication skills necessary to cultivate successful business opportunities.
This GCSE specification requires students to:
consider ethics and sustainability of business activity.
Students are also expected to develop the following skills:
personal skills in showing evidence of progression
interpersonal skills in communication and group work
Specification: Business (9-1) – J204
Business 01: Business activity, marketing and people
Students are introduced to business concepts and issues concerning the activities of a business. They explore the purpose and role of a business from spotting an opportunity through to the growth of an established business. They also look at the role of marketing and human resources.
Business 02: Operations, finance and influences on business
Students have a closer look at the role of operations and finance in business activity. Operations include production processes, quality of goods and services, customer service, and working with suppliers. Finance covers its role, its sources, costs, profit and loss, cash and cash flow.
They also explore how business responds to external influences, such as ethical and environmental considerations, the economic climate and globalisation, and the interdependent nature of business.
Both Business 01 and 02 have an 80 Mark, 1 Hour 30 Minutes paper (50% of total GCSE)

Physical Education
Physical Education
The PE and Games curriculum provides opportunities for students to learn purposeful practical activities that will lead to their own positive physical, social, mental and emotional growth. The overriding aim of the PE and Games Department at Canbury School is to instil in students a lifelong love of being physically active.
Department Objectives
To encourage responsibility for one’s own learning.
Curriculum
The school offers a PE and Games curriculum to all students. Games lessons are delivered in the afternoon, with a variety of off-site sporting activities. PE lessons are taught on-site making use of the indoor and outdoor space at the school.
Games
PE
Academic PE
As an option at Year 10 students at Canbury have the chance to select the BTEC Level 1/ 2 Tech Award in Sport as one of their KS4 options. This is a two-year course, where students will have three one-hour lessons of BTEC Sport per week.
Competitive Sport
Students at Canbury have a full calendar of inclusive, competitive sports to participate in throughout the year. An extensive inter house sporting competition is run including cross country, basketball, football and an annual Sports Day in the summer.
Canbury is also part of the Surrey Special Schools Sports Association (SSSSA) which offers termly inter-school sporting tournaments for our students in football, badminton, netball, dance and yoga, unihoc and cricket.
Extracurricular activities
There are a vast array of sporting extracurricular activities for students to participate in at Canbury. There is a weekly multi-sports session which includes a range of sports such as self- defence, fencing and shooting sessions, delivered by outside coaches.

Careers & Work Experience Board
We have a range of business and charities that we work with to offer work experience, careers advice and job opportunities.
We will regularly update this page – if you would like to feature or have any questions please email: [email protected]
Our new careers board at school will have a rotating industry focus, highlighting different career options.
The link to further details is below and we have also added some useful links around careers, apprenticeships and work experience.
Sustainability & Renewable Energy

School Governors
To contact any of our Governors, please direct your email to [email protected]
Mr. Rupert Marks (Chair of Governors, Finance)
Rupert Marks began his career trading in the global energy and commodity markets. In the past decade, he has focused on working in the non-for-proft sector and is now Chief Operating Officer for a medical charity, as well as being a trustee for other charitable organisations, including Blind in Business who help people who are blind or have partial sight, into work. He has been a governor at Canbury since September 2021 and also sits on the finance committee. His son Luca was a student at Canbury and enjoyed many happy years there. Rupert lives locally and says he feels a very special bond to the school and is delighted to support it in any way he can.
Ms. Louise Clancy (Co-Chair of Governors, Special Education Needs and Disabilities)
Louise has worked in education for over 30 years. The last 11 years specifically in Special Educational Needs and Disability. Now retired, Louise continues to support schools, families and young people by volunteering with SEND charities alongside working as a Magistrate. Louise has been involved with Canbury since 2014 and is delighted to be able to continue supporting this very special school.
Mrs Rosie O'Malley (Marketing)
Rosie spent the bulk of her career at Unilever, where she focused on marketing and strategy roles, driven to solve real people’s real problems with innovative product solutions. In 2017, she left the corporate world behind to focus on caring for her daughter, Alannah, who has a chromosome condition, and to be a bit more present as she joined and settled into Canbury school. As Alannah found her feet at school and began to thrive, Rosie went back to some freelance marketing work, alongside a Trustee role on the charity CLEFT. Rosie is also a qualified yoga teacher and is currently studying to qualify as a Counsellor. Rosie is delighted to have the opportunity to continue to support this school, which gave so much to her daughter.
Mrs. Celia Patterson (Health and Safety & SEND)
Celia Patterson has been a governor since May 2022. Her career path started in television production and she currently runs her own holiday letting business in the South West. She was a joint founder of the charity Skybadger, supporting children with disabilities. Both Celia’s sons, Oscar and Felix, were students at Canbury. Her focus is Special Educational Needs.
Dr Elyse Waites (Safeguarding and Pastoral)
Elyse Waites has more than 15 years experience of working in the pastoral side of education. She has a particular interest in building resilience and supporting the emotional development of young people alongside their academic studies. A current Deputy Head at a South East London independent school, she joined the governing body in 2022 and says she particularly enjoys meeting the Canbury students.
